name: Question 11
worked_solution:
We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=({log}_{2}⁡x)^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2{log}_{2}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{2}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={({log}_{2}⁡x)}^{2}(x)-\int (x)(\frac{2{log}_{2}⁡x}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{({log}_{2}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int {log}_{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate  $\int {log}_{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u={log}_{2}⁡x\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2} \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=1\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \,\text{d}x=x.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {log}_{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =({log}_{2}⁡x)(x)-\int (x)(\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{2}⁡x-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\int \,\text{d}x \\  & =x{log}_{2}⁡x-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+D,\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant.

So we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({log}_{2}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & =x{({log}_{2}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}(x{log}_{2}⁡x-\frac{x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+D) \\  & =x{({log}_{2}⁡x)}^{2}-\frac{2x{log}_{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}+\frac{2x}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{x{ln}^{2}⁡x}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}-\frac{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}+\frac{2x}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}+C \\  & =\frac{x}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}({ln}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+2)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-\frac{2D}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula ${log}_{2}⁡x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}.$

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e}({log}_{2}⁡x)^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{x}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}({ln}^{2}⁡x-2\operatorname{ln}⁡x+2)]}_{1}^{e} \\  & =\frac{e}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}({ln}^{2}⁡e-2\operatorname{ln}⁡e+2)-\frac{1}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}({ln}^{2}⁡1-2\operatorname{ln}⁡1+2) \\  & =\frac{e}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}-\frac{2}{{ln}^{2}⁡2} \\  & =\frac{e-2}{{ln}^{2}⁡2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Evaluate ∫1e(log2⁡x)2dx.

a
 e−1ln⁡2
b
 2e+1ln2⁡2
c
 e+2ln2⁡2
d
 2e−1ln⁡2
e
 e−2ln2⁡2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define u=(log2⁡x)2⟹dudx=2log2⁡xxln⁡2dvdx=1⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫dx=x.

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get ∫(log2⁡x)2dx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(log2⁡x)2(x)−∫(x)(2log2⁡xxln⁡2)dx=x(log2⁡x)2−2ln⁡2∫log2⁡xdx.

We use integration by parts once again to evaluate ∫log2⁡(x)dx. We take u=log2⁡x⟹dudx=1xln⁡2dvdx=1⟹v=∫dvdxdx=∫dx=x.

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives ∫log2⁡xdx=∫udvdxdx=uv−∫vdudxdx=(log2⁡x)(x)−∫(x)(1xln⁡2)dx=xlog2⁡x−1ln⁡2∫dx=xlog2⁡x−xln⁡2+D, where D is an integral constant.

So we have ∫(log2⁡x)2dx=x(log2⁡x)2−2ln⁡2(xlog2⁡x−xln⁡2+D)=x(log2⁡x)2−2xlog2⁡xln⁡2+2xln2⁡2+C=xln2⁡xln2⁡2−2xln⁡xln2⁡2+2xln2⁡2+C=xln2⁡2(ln2⁡x−2ln⁡x+2)+C, where C=−2Dln⁡2.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula log2⁡x=ln⁡xln⁡2.

Finally then, we can work out the definite integral: ∫1e(log2⁡x)2dx=[xln2⁡2(ln2⁡x−2ln⁡x+2)]1e=eln2⁡2(ln2⁡e−2ln⁡e+2)−1ln2⁡2(ln2⁡1−2ln⁡1+2)=eln2⁡2−2ln2⁡2=e−2ln2⁡2.
